part: Coverage grid in the household store, with a monthly job and extra weekly jobs before each break
problem: The card builds a grid (rows per date range and child, four statuses), a monthly job from January to May and more weekly jobs before every break, on top of five other cards. Its own caveat says a shared spreadsheet does the grid, and nothing on record says the family has children of camp age or that both parents work on no-school days.
checked: Card caveats 1 and 5 and depends_on (F031, F009 or F010, F018, F019, F007, F002). Fact sheet: the config repo records no children, and schools, activities, grandparents and work patterns were never stated. The roadmap has no childcare feature. The one demand source is a university blog about parents in general.

proposal.text: Do you want Happy to hold the no-school coverage grid at all? Default: no. Keep the grid where you keep it today, set registration dates as ordinary reminders (F007) and ask the research helper for camp options when you want them (F019); drop the store rows and both scheduled jobs. If you do want it, start with one monthly text and no pre-break weekly jobs.

loses: The 'N of 10 weeks still open' count and a grid Happy can be asked about.

part: Tax-time receipts list (amount and provider per receipt, taxpayer-number chase, February totals)
problem: A tax-paperwork job was attached to a childcare planner: Happy reads receipt photos, stores amounts per provider and in February lists totals and missing taxpayer numbers. It is not needed for planning cover, and receipt photos go to the cloud model unscreened.
checked: Card how, safety (the privacy gate screens text PDFs only) and caveat 4 ('for the preparer, not tax advice'). The only source is IRS Publication 503, which says what can qualify, not that a family wants this tracked. Fact sheet: nothing about day camps, tax preparation or children's ages.

proposal.text: Remove the receipts and February tax list from this card. A parent who wants one fact kept can say 'remember we paid X to camp Y' (F041).

loses: The February per-provider totals and the reminder to ask a camp for its taxpayer number.

part: Three briefs per parent (evening, Sunday week-ahead, weekday morning): six jobs
problem: The card schedules three different texts per parent and then needs caveats to manage their collisions: two texts within ninety minutes on Sunday, and two at 07:00 once the mail digest runs. Tony never named a time of day for any text, and the morning leg also needs a sunset calculation the weather tool does not have.
checked: Card how and caveats 1, 3 and 4. Fact sheet: preferred times of day were never stated. Roadmap: the only scheduled text it plans is the 7:00 mail digest (M4); it has no calendar brief. r7 index: the 07:00 mail digest (G015) is now wave B, the same wave as this card.

proposal.text: One evening job per parent, Sunday to Thursday at 19:30, calendar and weather only. Its Sunday run is told to cover the week ahead. Drop the separate 18:00 Sunday job and the 07:00 morning brief from the card.

loses: A separate morning text with today's calendar, and the week-ahead arriving ninety minutes earlier on Sunday.

part: Household-store read on the week-ahead and morning legs (items due, trash day, open school deadlines)
problem: Two of the three briefs read a second data source that does not exist yet, through a tool name the card itself lists as untested, and F010 writes school-deadline rows into it only so that the brief can read them back. Trash day and a deadline can simply be calendar entries or reminders, which the brief and F007 already handle.
checked: Card unverified items 3 and 4 ('the deadlines input does not exist yet; its shape is a design choice'; the home-store tool glob is untested), depends_on, and caveat 8 (the store read is also proposed for the evening brief only to check a mute). F010 depends_on last line. F031 card. No roadmap rule asks for a store behind the brief.

proposal.text: Briefs read the family calendar and the weather, nothing else. Whatever the family wants in a brief goes on the calendar (trash day as a repeating event, a deadline as an entry) or is a reminder. Remove F031 from this card's dependencies and the school-deadline rows from F010.

loses: An 'items due' line fed from store rows, and a mute by chat becomes best effort for the brief (Tony can disable the job for a holiday).

part: Email-derived dates fed into the week-ahead from a separate mail-agent job using llm-task
problem: The card plans a second job on the mail agent to extract dates and hand them to the brief, and says the hand-off 'still has to be designed'. With mail now in wave B, each parent already gets mail dates twice from the mail agent itself (the 07:00 digest and the 16:00 school digest), so this is a third route for the same dates.
checked: Card how (last but one sentence), caveat 5 and depends_on, which still say 'G015, wave C' although the r7 index puts G015 and F051 in wave B. Roadmap security table: a mail agent's only output is its scheduled announcement to its owner, so any hand-off into the parent's main agent is new plumbing against that row. Fact sheet: Tony said the school digest becomes trivial once the inbox is read.

proposal.text: Remove the mail-derived-dates branch. Mail dates stay in the two mail digests; a parent who wants one on the calendar says yes to F010's offer.

loses: The Sunday text will not repeat deadlines that arrived by email unless they were put on the calendar.

part: The [T]/[S] driver tag on calendar events and the per-child routines-and-gear table
problem: 'Who drives' and 'what to pack' depend on two family habits that an agent invented: parents tagging every event with a driver, and a gear table kept in Happy's instructions. The card says these two lines are what its brief adds over Google's own daily digest.
checked: Card caveats 2 and 7 and unverified item 1 ('no source can vouch that both adults will keep it up'). Fact sheet: no children, routines or activities are recorded, and which calendar the family shares was never stated. Config repo family file: no such table.

proposal.text: Do the two of you want to tag calendar events with who drives, and to keep a pack list in Happy's instructions? Default: no. The first brief is tomorrow's events, the forecast and any active weather alert; driver and packing lines are added only when you ask for them.

loses: The 'who drives' and 'pack shin guards' lines.

part: Part 2, the calendar write: an in-house write server around gog, its own write token, an approval hook, attendee stripping
problem: To put dates on the family calendar the card needs four new parts and a two-step confirmation on iMessage (a yes, then a typed /approve with an id) that has never been tried in Basic mode. The card's own caveat calls this the optional, later step that 'need not be built' if the parents add events on the phone or in Gemini.
checked: Card how, caveats 3, 5, 6 and 8, unverified items 3 to 6. gog's MCP page (gogcli.sh/mcp, opened in this run) lists no calendar write tool, so the wrapper really is new code. Roadmap approvals row requires an approval enforced in code for actions, so the hook cannot be thinned if the write is built. Fact sheet: the calendar choice (Google or iCloud) is still open and Tony has not asked for calendar writes.

proposal.text: Make the card Part 1 only: Happy lists the dates in full and, after a yes, sets reminders (F002 plus F007, a prompt rule, effort S). Move the calendar write out of wave B with no date; revisit only if a parent asks for it after using the reminders.

loses: Happy cannot put a season schedule on the shared calendar; a parent adds events on the phone.

part: Second calendar route: a plugin that sends a tap-to-add calendar file, built only if a phone test passes
problem: The card carries two alternative ways to reach the calendar. The only report found for this one says a calendar file did not offer to add the event, yet the branch stays, with a plugin and an untested outbound-file check behind it.
checked: Card caveat 4 and unverified items 1 and 2 (an Apple forum post and a 2022 blog, neither about Messages; outbound media check untested). No roadmap line or statement from Tony asks for it.

proposal.text: Before anything is designed, Tony sends one calendar file from Messages on the Mac to each parent's phone by hand and taps it (five minutes, no code). If the phone offers to add the event, this is the only calendar route and the write server, token and hook are never built. If not, delete the branch.

loses: nothing

part: Optional llm-task call that returns the dates as a schema-checked list
problem: A second model call, a plugin switch and two config lists are offered for something the reply model already does in the same turn. A checked list only matters when code consumes it, and in Part 1 a person reads the dates and says yes.
checked: Card how and its llm-task source ('this feature does not require it'); unverified item 8 (whether llm-task runs with an empty tool surface on Happy's provider is unknown).

proposal.text: Remove the llm-task option from this card. Revisit only if a calendar write that takes a list is ever built.

loses: nothing

part: A new group-chat agent with mention gating and a zero history limit, re-opening iMessage groups
problem: A new shared agent and a change to the security baseline are added so that Happy can answer weather and web-search questions in a three-way chat. Each parent can already ask the same question one to one, and Tony has not asked for a group chat.
checked: Roadmap M1 deliverables ('groups disabled') and S1 ('groups off'); live config has the group policy set to disabled. Card caveat 1 says this is 'a change to that baseline for Tony to approve'. Fact sheet: whether Jordan wants any of this was never stated. The demand source is an OpenClaw example for a different channel, which shows it is possible, not that this family needs it.

proposal.text: Do you and Jordan want a three-way chat with Happy? Default: no. Leave groups off, take the card out of wave A and park it under Later.

loses: Both parents seeing one answer in a shared thread.

part: The group as 'one place for shared announcements' so a watcher needs one job instead of two
problem: A second purpose was added to the group chat to save one scheduled job per watcher. Two jobs made from the same registry line are far less machinery than a group, and the card's own caveat says a group text cannot respect one parent's mute.
checked: Card caveat 5; F018 caveat 4 and depends_on ('one job per parent with its own state file, or one job delivering to the group'); MKT-06 and G009 depends_on, which also lean on the group. Roadmap replies row: scheduled jobs deliver only to their owner. Installed docs channels/imessage/media.md list a chat id as an outbound address, separately from the inbound group policy.

proposal.text: Announcements for both parents are two jobs, one per parent, each with its own state file. Remove F006 from the dependencies of F018, MKT-06 and G009. If one shared text is ever wanted, first test whether a job can deliver to the group's chat id while inbound groups stay off, which needs no agent.

loses: nothing (two texts, one per phone, instead of one group text)

part: Stand-alone conflict watcher: its own reading credential, both parents sharing a calendar as free/busy, a state file, a tagging rule
problem: The watch needs a separate sign-in, a sharing step by each parent, a script, a seen-list and a written rule for which events count, and its own caveats say it cries wolf without the rule and cannot see most work calendars. It assumes each parent keeps a personal Google calendar, which nobody has said.
checked: Card how, caveats 2, 4 and 6, unverified items 1, 3 and 6 (gog not installed; free/busy sharing untested; work calendars may be invisible). Fact sheet: which calendar the family shares and whether both parents use it were never stated; the Google-or-iCloud decision is still open. The demand source is a competing product's feature page.

proposal.text: Do each of you keep your own appointments on a Google calendar Happy could see as 'busy'? Default: no stand-alone watch. Add one sentence to the evening brief (F014): say so when two family-calendar events overlap. If you answer yes and still want the watch, run it once a day in the morning rather than every few hours.

loses: Clashes with something that is only on a parent's own or work calendar, and a warning between briefs.

part: 'Who covers?' follow-up through the ask-and-relay step of G009
problem: The text already ends with the question and both parents receive it. Wiring it to the relay adds a pending-requests table, a reply-matching plugin and an expiry job so that Happy can carry an answer the parents can give each other directly.
checked: Card how (last clause) and depends_on; G009 how (the relay is 'an optional second step': a table in the household store, a before_dispatch plugin and a one-shot job). No roadmap rule or statement from Tony asks for it.

proposal.text: Keep the line as plain text and remove the relay hook-up and the G009 relay dependency from this card.

loses: Happy does not record who said they would cover.

part: Place lookup: a Google Cloud project with billing, an API key in a host-side wrapper, a budget alert, and a choice between two Google connections
problem: Opening hours and ratings bring a billed Google account, an in-house wrapper and an open choice between two products, one of which may not return hours at all. The card says the plan can be built from web pages and the forecast in the meantime, and that the maps app on the phone is quicker for 'is it open'.
checked: Card caveats 3, 8 and 9, unverified items 4 to 6 (prices not read; goplaces not installed; the hosted server's status unknown). Roadmap M3 names the hosted Maps server as a deliverable, but section 9 has no row for it, so it is not marked as Tony's own choice. F019 already gives the research helper web search and page reading.

proposal.text: Build the planner on the research helper alone (web search, venue pages, the home forecast). After five real plans, add a place lookup only if hours were missing or wrong; then use the hosted server the roadmap names, with no in-house wrapper, provided a first query shows it returns opening hours.

loses: Structured hours and ratings; the plan relies on what venue pages say.

part: Optional Friday 16:00 'this weekend near us' text
problem: An unprompted weekly text sits inside a card about plans made on request. The card itself says Google's scheduled actions already do this, that round 1 removed a similar brief for that reason, and that it should be built last and only if a parent asks.
checked: Card caveat 7 and history r5. Fact sheet: no parent asked for it and no preferred time for texts was stated.

proposal.text: Remove the Friday job from the card. A parent who wants ideas texts 'what's on this weekend?'.

loses: A weekend-ideas text nobody has to ask for.

part: Paperwork line for trips abroad (passport dates from the renewals table, consent-letter pointer)
problem: A travel-documents check was folded into the planner in review. It makes two agents write one answer, raised the card's risk because passport dates and names are now involved, and repeats what the renewals look-ahead already does. Nothing says the family travels abroad with children.
checked: Card history r2 (CRT-14 folded in; 'the risk rises to medium'), how (last sentence), depends_on (F063), caveat 6. F063 already gives about nine months' notice before a passport expires. Fact sheet: passports and children were never stated.

proposal.text: Remove the paperwork line and the F063 dependency. Passport expiry stays in the renewals look-ahead; a parent can ask 'do the kids need a consent letter?' as an ordinary question.

loses: A passport and consent-letter reminder at the moment a trip is planned.

part: Storm-alert watcher: a script polling every 30 minutes round the clock, with id dedup, a chore checklist and an urgent class
problem: Happy's weather tool already returns active alerts for home with every forecast, so the evening brief carries them, and the phones already notify about government weather alerts. The card's own caveat says the watcher gives no earlier notice; what it adds is a checklist and a school-night line, at the cost of a script, an untested dedup rule and night-time texts.
checked: Config repo plugins/home-weather/nws.js: each forecast call also fetches active alerts for the home point and puts them first in the answer. F014 how: the evening brief holds that tool. Card caveats 2 and 10, unverified item 1, and its Apple support source. Fact sheet: Tony's own example of a monitor was school email; storm alerts were not asked for.

proposal.text: No storm script. Add one sentence to the evening brief: when an alert is active, name it and, on a school night, say to watch for the school's own notice. Leave the moment-of-issue alert to the phones.

loses: A text from Happy at the moment an alert is issued, between two briefs.

part: Recall watch: two scripts (CPSC daily, FDA twice a day) matched against four family keyword lists
problem: The match depends on lists of owned items, allergens, staples and medicines that the family would have to write and keep current, and the card says substring matching gives false alarms and misses. Both agencies offer their own email sign-ups, and from wave B Happy reads the inbox those emails arrive in.
checked: Card caveats 2, 8 and 9, depends_on last line, sources (CPSC and FDA sign-up pages). Fact sheet: allergies and medications were never stated; Tony moved whole-inbox reading to wave B. G015 card: a 07:00 digest of each parent's inbox.

proposal.text: No recall scripts and no keyword lists. One parent signs up for the two agencies' emails, and the mail digest (G015) gets one sentence: mention a recall notice that looks relevant.

loses: A model-free match against a list of what the family owns; the digest's model reads the agency emails instead, as it reads all other mail.

part: Team-schedule watcher (hourly) and generic changed-page watcher (every 6 hours)
problem: Two general-purpose scripts are planned before anyone has named a team feed or a page to watch. The card says team apps push a change faster, a hash watch fires on changes that do not matter, and a first check of which sites even publish a feed is still outstanding.
checked: Card caveats 2 and 7, unverified items 4 and 6 to 8, depends_on ('a first check of which of the family's sites publish a feed'). Fact sheet: activities, teams and school platforms were never stated. Card sources: the team apps document subscribing their schedule into Google Calendar, which F009 and the brief then read.

proposal.text: Write neither script now. When a parent names one feed or page, subscribe a team schedule into the family calendar first (no code); write a single script for that one page only if that is not enough.

loses: Nothing today; later, a 'game moved' text for a same-day change, which the team app's own push covers.

part: Each script checks every address itself (https, public host)
problem: A general address checker is asked of scripts that fetch only addresses Tony registered, show the result to no model and print a fixed line. The existing weather plugin handles the same concern by pinning one host.
checked: Card caveat 5 and safety ('requests go only to addresses Tony registered'; 'no model reads any feed'). F083 how ('keep the api.weather.gov host pin'). Roadmap LAN rule is written for the research browser, where page content reaches a model.

proposal.text: Each script is pinned to its one registered host and refuses redirects to any other host. No general public-address checker.

loses: nothing

part: Workarounds for the notification policy repeated in four cards
problem: Because the planned policy drops a text instead of holding it, four cards each add their own fix: run only inside allowed hours, an urgent class for storms, a loss 'written into each job's charter', an extra store read on the brief, and limits on what may go to the group. Tony never asked for quiet hours or a daily cap.
checked: F018 caveat 10 and depends_on, MKT-06 caveat 5, F014 caveat 8, F006 caveat 5; G001 card description ('dropped, not sent later'). Fact sheet: quiet hours, preferred times and a daily cap were never stated. The roadmap has no notification-policy rule.

proposal.text: Do you want a daily cap and quiet hours enforced by a plugin in the first build? Default: no. Every scheduled job simply gets a daytime hour in its schedule line, and the policy is revisited only if the texts turn out to be too many. The four cards then lose these workarounds and their dependency on G001.

loses: An enforced cap and a mute by chat; a pause is Tony disabling a job.
